Region nadále sužují strukturální bezpečnostní problémy včetně organizovaného zločinu v Andách a na pobřeží, zatímco trhy s komoditami reagují na globální geopolitické vlivy a kolísání cel.

The region continues to grapple with structural security issues including organized crime in the Andes and coastal trafficking, while commodity markets react to global geopolitical forces and tariff fluctuations.

recommendations.reason_en: Arabica coffee prices hit record levels driven by tariff volatility and U.S.-Colombia trade friction. The agricultural sector remains robust but faces tightening global scrutiny regarding deforestation and environmental compliance.

articles.title: Brazil’s victory for the planet and democracy: seven lessons from Lula’s win
articles.summary:
The trouncing of the far right provides a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France

Thank you, Brazil, for demonstrating how the far right can be trounced while protection for the Amazon is strengthened. In a world where nature and democracy appeared to be bleeding out in tandem, voters and forest defenders in this global south powerhouse have shown it is possible to staunch the flow. This should provide much needed inspiration and, more practically, a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France.

The astonishing comeback victory of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Sunday’s presidential runoff against his extreme right challenger Flavío Bolsonaro has brought oceans of rapturous supporters on to the streets, while also thrilling conservationists, climate activists and social justice campaigners across the world.

articles.summary:
The far-right candidate was supposed to claim the presidency, but Brazilian voters had other ideas

For Donald Trump, Brazil’s presidential election was meant to represent the crest of the “orange wave” – a three-year surge of rightwing triumphs that has reshaped Latin American politics in the US president’s tangerine-hued image.

The far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, was supposed to claim the presidency on Sunday, bringing the region’s biggest democracy and economy into Trump’s orbit, after similar victories in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Honduras, Ecuador and Peru – not to mention the capture of Venezuela’s government after the country was invaded in January.
